name: shweta_governed_handover
title: Governed handover when someone leaves
author: shweta
desc:
Somebody leaves the company. This workflow reports everything they own across Leads, Deals, Contacts and Accounts, waits for one human approval, reassigns the whole book in a single governed batch, and confirms the change is recorded in a tamper-evident ledger.

The point is the middle step. plan_handover fingerprints the exact set of records it is about to move. apply_handover re-reads that set, re-hashes it, and REFUSES if anything moved while the approval was sitting in the queue - so a record edited between review and execution stops the write rather than being silently swept up in it. A CRM has no undo, and this is the gap that ordinary automation leaves open.

Every step runs through the RailCall airlock and produces a signed receipt. The final step verifies the local change ledger, which is hash-chained: each entry carries the fingerprint of the one before it, so editing or removing an entry breaks every link after it.

Honest about limits: the ledger is tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof, and it records changes made through this module only. Somebody editing directly in the Zoho UI is invisible to it.

Trigger contract: supply from_user and to_user as email addresses of Zoho CRM users.

Dependencies: requires shweta/zoho-crm v0.6.1 or later, with the zoho vault entry configured (client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, token_url, instance_url). Run zoho.verify_connection first - it names any missing scope and which commands it blocks. [contest:2026Q3]
